newsitem.title: UK: Rover sees long term stg strength as problem.
newsitem.headline: Rover sees long term stg strength as problem.

text.p: German owned Rover group, the British car maker, said a strong sterling exchange rate would be a problem in the longer term.
Walter Hasselkus, chief executive of BMW owned Rover, told German journalists on Thursday that sterling exchange rates of 2.70 to 2.80 marks "would be a problem for Rover and the British industry."
The mark's recent decline against most currencies, including sterling and the dollar, has benefited German exporters but made foreign products more expensive for Germans.
But Hasselkus said Rover would not be impacted by the situation immediately as the group had largely hedged its currency positions through the end of 1998.
Hasselkus also said he did not expect the pound to continue trading at its current strong levels.

If the currency were to remain strong however, Rover could attempt to minimise the negative effects by buying more parts abroad, Hasselkus said, stressing that the situation should not be viewed with inappropriate concern.
"England as a production centre is not up for discussion," Hasselkus said.
Sterling was trading around 2.74 marks in midday trading on Thursday.
